verifications.claim: The "No Tax on Tips" policy is implemented via the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the “No Tax on Tips” provision of the OBBBA (R1); One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed into law on July 4, 2025 (R3); “No Tax on Tips” provision of the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) (R4); “no tax on tips” deduction created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly attribute the policy to the OBBBA or equivalent naming, signed in 2025.

verifications.claim: The "No Tax on Tips" policy allows eligible workers in over 70 tipped occupations to deduct up to $25,000 in voluntarily received cash tips from their federal income taxes from 2025–2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: eligible workers in more than seventy qualifying occupations ... deduct up to $25,000 per year in tips ... “qualified tips” must be “cash tips” voluntarily paid ... taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029 (R1); Maximum annual deduction is $25,000 ... qualified tips received in certain qualified occupations (R2); list of nearly 70 occupations ... up to $25,000 annually ... Voluntary: Tips freely given ... Cash-based ... from January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2028 (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely match occupation count (>70), deduction amount, voluntary cash tips, federal income tax, and exact years.

verifications.claim: The deduction excludes automatic gratuities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: excludes automatic gratuities (R1); Mandatory service charges, automatic gratuities ... do not qualify (R3); service charges, automatic gratuities ... are not qualified tips (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in multiple sources confirm exclusion.

verifications.claim: The deduction applies to employees in food service, hospitality, and personal services who report their tips.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Beverage and Food Service ... Hospitality and Guest Services ... Personal Services ... (R1); Employees and self-employed individuals may deduct qualified tips ... such as wait staff ... (food service), salon workers (personal services) (R2); Food and Beverage Service Occupations ... Personal Service Occupations ... Properly reported: Tips must be reported to your employer (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources list matching sectors and confirm applicability to employees who report tips; broader inclusion of self-employed does not contradict.

verifications.claim: Workers must be in a "customarily tipped" occupation to be eligible for the "No Tax on Tips" policy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: occupation[s] that customarily and regularly receive[] tips (R1); certain qualified occupations, such as ... who customarily and regularly receive tips (R2); occupations that “customarily and regularly received tips” before December 31, 2024 (R3); occupation that “customarily and regularly” received tips as of December 31, 2024 (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources require 'customarily and regularly receive tips' occupations.

verifications.claim: Customarily tipped occupations include restaurant servers, bartenders, hairdressers, valets, and taxi drivers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 101 Bartenders 102 Wait Staff ... 603 Barbers, Hairdressers ... 801 Parking and Valet Attendants 802 Taxi and Rideshare Drivers (R1); Bartenders, waiters ... Hairdressers, barbers ... Taxi drivers ... valets, parking attendants (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Exact occupations listed in sources.

verifications.claim: Only voluntary cash tips (including credit card tips) qualify for the deduction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: “qualified tips” must be “cash tips” voluntarily paid ... tips paid by electronic payments, checks, debit cards (R1); “Qualified tips” are voluntary cash or charged tips (R2); Voluntary: Tips freely given ... Cash-based: This includes physical cash, checks, credit/debit card tips (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on voluntary and cash (including credit card/electronic).

verifications.claim: Automatic service charges for large parties are not included in qualified tips.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: example of a restaurant with a menu that specifies an automatic 18 percent charge for parties of six or more. Such a charge would not be a qualified tip (R1); Automatic service fees for large parties at a restaurant cannot be deducted (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct examples and statements confirm exclusion.

verifications.claim: The deduction limit is up to $25,000 per tax year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: deduct up to $25,000 per year (R1); Maximum annual deduction is $25,000 (R2); capped at $25,000 annually (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent across sources.

verifications.claim: The deduction benefit phases out for individuals with a modified adjusted gross income over $150,000 ($300,000 for joint filers).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: phases out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income over $150,000 ($300,000 for joint filers) (R2); Phase-out begins at $150,000 modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) Married filing jointly: $300,000 MAGI (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Exact thresholds and filing status matched.

verifications.claim: Tips must be reported to the employer for payroll tax purposes to qualify for the deduction.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: qualified tips paid to them in 2025 that are included on Form W-2 ... or reported directly by them on Form 4137 (R2); Tips must be reported to your employer on Form 4070 ... appear on your W-2 (R3); reporting tips to your employer, and you must report all tips over $20 per employer per month (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Supported for employees, but self-employed report differently (no employer), so not universally precise.

verifications.claim: The 2025 standard deduction is $15,750 for individuals.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: $15,750 for individuals ... for tax year 2025 (R5); $15,750 (single filer) in 2025 (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match.

verifications.claim: The 2025 standard deduction is $31,500 for married couples.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: $31,500 for couples married filing jointly for tax year 2025 (R5); $31,500 (joint filers) in 2025 (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match.

verifications.claim: Individuals earning less than the standard deduction owe no federal income tax.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Taxpayers who earn less than the standard deduction — $15,750 for individuals ... don’t have to file a federal income tax return.
verifications.reasoning: Implies no tax owed; standard deduction reduces taxable income to zero if income below it.

verifications.claim: The IRS has identified over 70 occupations in sectors such as food/beverage, hospitality, personal services, and entertainment that qualify for the deduction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: expanded list of seventy-one specified occupations ... Beverage and Food Service ... Hospitality and Guest Services ... Personal Services ... Entertainment and Events (R1); over 70 occupations ... Beverage and food service ... Hospitality and guest services ... Personal services ... Entertainment and events (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact count and matching sectors.

verifications.claim: The tax deduction for tips is valid for the 2025 through 2028 tax years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029 (R1); from January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2028 (R3); available for the 2025–2028 tax years (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Precise timeframe confirmed.

verifications.claim: Several states, including Arizona, California, Georgia, and others, have proposed their own versions of "no tax on tips" legislation.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention state proposals or specific states like Arizona, California, Georgia.

verifications.claim: The "No Tax on Tips" policy does not exempt tips from Social Security or Medicare taxes, only federal income tax.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: still subject to federal income tax withholding, Social Security taxes, and Medicare taxes (FICA) (R3); only applies to federal income tax, so workers’ tips will still be subject to payroll taxes like those that fund Social Security and Medicare (R5); you may still have to pay payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security and Medicare) (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct confirmations.

verifications.claim: Automatic gratuities are treated as taxable wages.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Qualified tips do not include automatic gratuities or surcharges (R1); Mandatory service charges, automatic gratuities ... do not qualify ... Your tips are still subject to federal income tax withholding (R3); service charges, automatic gratuities ... are not qualified tips (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Not qualified for deduction means remain taxable as wages/income.

verifications.claim: The deduction is only applicable if the tips are officially reported.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: qualified tips ... included on Form W-2, Form 1099-NEC ... or reported directly ... on Form 4137 (R2); Properly reported: Tips must be reported to your employer ... appear on your W-2 ... Form 4137 (R3); only qualified tips that are separately reported on Form W-2 ... will be deductible (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Deduction based on reported tips across forms.
